WEC.scenario_basis: Starting 2026 EPS guide midpoint $5.56; bear EPS growth 3%/yr (equity-issuance dilution drag, regulatory lag) + P/E compresses to 15x + 3.5% dividend; base EPS growth 7.5%/yr (per management's guided 7-8% through 2030) + P/E holds ~18x + 3.5% dividend; bull EPS growth 9%/yr (large-load upside beyond plan) + P/E expands to 20x + 3.5% dividend.
kill_criteria: Full-year EPS guidance cut (vs. maintained/raised) at any quarterly release
Announced large-load (data-center) capacity commitments reduced or cancelled by a named large customer (e.g. Microsoft, Vantage)
Rating-agency downgrade below the current A-/Baa1-area profile, or FFO/debt below stated 15% (S&P) / 16% (Moody's) targets for two consecutive periods
Common-equity issuance in a given year exceeds the guided $5.3-5.7B five-year pace by >25%
Adverse rate-case order in WI/IL/MI/MN reducing authorized ROE below ~9.5% or disallowing material planned capex
key_adverse_facts: Financing the $37.5B five-year capital plan requires ~$1.1B/year of common-equity issuance (2026), a real, ongoing per-share dilution offset to the guided 7-8% EPS growth

Approximate net debt/EBITDA ~6.1x (not the ideal metric for a regulated utility, but directionally high); the more sector-appropriate FFO/debt targets (S&P >15%, Moody's CFO-pre-WC >16%) and the A-/Baa1 rating were sourced via secondary aggregation this pass, not independently confirmed against the rating agencies' own releases

Large-load demand figures (2.6 GW, 3.5 GW through 2030) are company investor-material planning figures, not fully in-service, signed load -- data-center buildout plans have seen delays/cancellations industry-wide
Q2 2026 guidance was maintained, not raised -- the addendum's raise/maintain/cut framework should record this honestly rather than spun as a beat
